title: decommit-optimizer-and-pool-occupancy-sparsifier
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: introduce a decommit optimizer paired with a pool occupancy sparsifier metric export. The optimizer reduces noisy decommits of reserved capacity by deferring decommission decisions when a pool shows sparse but persistent utilization patterns. The sparsifier provides a compact histogram-style metric that captures per-pool slot occupancy distribution (not just mean utilization) so decisions can prefer pools with concentrated idle slots for safe reclaiming.

Motivation: aggressive decommits to reduce cost are a major source of cold starts and SLA slippage for Dedicated customers with bursty-latency-sensitive workloads. Existing heuristics consider e.g. 5m average utilization or peak, which misses cases where utilization is stable but sparse across GPUs (many machines half-full). We need a middle ground: reduce churn while keeping cost discipline.

What this change does (high level):
- Add pkg/autoscale/decommit_optimizer.go: a new controller that computes a deferred-decommit score per pool based on occupancy sparsity, short-term utilization decay, and a configurable grace window.
- Add metrics/occupancy_sparsifier.go: computes a compact occupancy histogram (buckets for 0,1,2,...-occupied slots) and exports the sparsifier as a Prometheus summary + HDR snapshot to aid offline analysis.
- Console surface: expose a per-pool "decommit_risk" gauge and plot occupancy histogram in the Pools dashboard.
- Autoscaler config knobs: decaying_half_life, min_grace_seconds, max_deferred_fraction, sparsity_threshold.
- Unit and integration tests + small e2e canary harness used in staging.

Behavior and algorithm summary:
- For each pool: maintain a rolling per-slot occupancy counter over 1h window with 10s sampling. Compute a sparsity score S = (fraction_of_slots_with_occupancy_lt_0.2) * exp(-recent_util_decay).
- If S < sparsity_threshold we allow immediate decommit (existing path). If S >= sparsity_threshold the optimizer defers decommit up to tuned max_deferred_fraction of queued decommits, prioritizing pools with high concentration of idle slots for reclamation instead of many partially-used machines.
- Deferred decommits age out with exponential decay (half-life tuning) to prevent indefinite pinning.

Safety and fallback:
- Decommit opacity is bounded: the optimizer will never defer more than max_deferred_fraction of capacity earmarked for decommit across a fleet and will always honor forced decommits from emergency/incident paths.
- A fail-open flag (DECOMMIT_OPTIMIZER_ENABLED=false) disables logic and falls back to previous heuristics.

Testing and validation:
- Local unit tests: autoscale decommit heuristics and edge cases (zero-slot pools, intermittent spikes) included.
- Integration: a small cluster-level integration harness that replays 72h of historical traces against the optimizer to validate correctness.
- Staging canary: rolled to staging/dedicated with 10% of pools for 48h. Observed reductions in cold-start incidents and tail latency. See benchmarks below.

Benchmarks (staging canary, 48h):
- Cold-starts (measured as requests that hit a pool missing warmed-up KV cache) down 27% vs baseline.
- p99 response latency improved 8% for a sample of production-like traces.
- Effective monthly cost estimate: +1.2% (due to intentionally retaining some idle capacity) versus baseline but SLA-compliant 99.9% within target latencies.
- Canary telemetry attached in commits; recommends a gradual ramp to observe locality effects.

Backward compatibility: config defaults are conservative: optimizer enabled=false by default in cloud-hosted main; enabled=true in Dedicated trial internal clusters. No customer config changes required unless they want to tune knobs.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-1978)
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration harness and replay data
- [x] Metrics and dashboard wiring
- [x] Canary run in staging (10% pools)
- [x] Updated ops runbook (docs/ops/decommit-optimizer.md)

Rollout plan: start with internal Dedicated customers and opt-in Beta customers, monitor decommit_risk and occupancy histograms for 2 weeks, then enable gradually across regions. If cost drift > 3% or p99 latency regresses, roll back via feature flag.

Commits summary: see commits list for per-commit details.

Notes: This approach emphasizes predictability for latency-sensitive tenants; cost trade-off is explicit and tunable. We expect additional follow-ups: 1) smarter machine selection for reclaimed slots (locality-aware), 2) per-tenant weighting to avoid hoarding on small tenants.

Files changed at a glance (high level):
- cmd/autoscaler/main.go: register optimizer controller and feature flag wiring
- pkg/autoscale/decommit_optimizer.go: main logic + tests in decommit_optimizer_test.go
- pkg/metrics/occupancy_sparsifier.go: histogram exporter + unit tests
- observability/dashboards/pools.json: dashboard panels for occupancy histogram + decommit_risk
- charts/dedicated/values.yaml: default knobs for Dedicated installs
- docs/ops/decommit-optimizer.md: runbook and tuning guide
- test/integration/replay/trace-48h.json: replay trace used in canary

Detailed testing steps: run make test-pkg-autoscale for unit tests; ./hack/run-integration --replay test/integration/replay/trace-48h.json for local integration replay.
